subject.title: Provider key pools + bucket-aware cooldown/backoff on 429 (Gemini projects) to prevent retry storms

question: Should OpenClaw add a native generic provider key/profile quota-bucket routing contract for Gemini-style project quotas, and should that live in core provider/auth fallback or outside core as a sidecar/plugin seam?
rationale: The remaining work changes public config, auth-profile routing, cooldown scope, provider selection, secret handling, and upgrade behavior, so automation should not invent the product boundary or defaults.

options.title: Design Generic Bucket Routing
options.body: Define an additive provider/auth bucket metadata and cooldown contract, then implement Gemini as one consumer while keeping current flat rotation as the default.

options.title: Fold Into Provider-Pool Tracker
options.body: Treat this as a Gemini bucket acceptance criterion under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/41135 and close this only after maintainers explicitly consolidate that scope.

options.title: Keep External For Now
options.body: Recommend the linked sidecar/plugin-style approach until maintainers decide native bucket routing is worth the new config and state surface.

recommendation.title: Design Generic Bucket Routing
recommendation.body: Define an additive provider/auth bucket metadata and cooldown contract, then implement Gemini as one consumer while keeping current flat rotation as the default.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a provider/auth config and product-boundary decision, and steipete has the strongest adjacent history among the identified routing candidates.
